title: Air-fryer Korean-style wings
subtitle: Gochujang-glazed wings with sesame and spring onion.
excerpt: Crispy air-fried wings tossed in a sticky gochujang and honey glaze with sesame and spring onion. The sauce is sweet, hot, and deeply savoury. Serves two as a main or four as a snack.
sourceNotes: Korean fried chicken (yangnyeom chicken) is a popular dish in Korean cuisine and in Korean-American cooking. This version is adapted for the home air fryer, using gochujang paste for the characteristic sweet heat of the original without deep-frying.

content.text: Korean-style wings get their character from gochujang paste: fermented chilli, sticky, deeply savoury, and moderately hot. The wings go into the fryer plain and the sauce goes on at the end, the same two-stage method as honey garlic wings. The final two minutes in the fryer sets the glaze and chars the edges slightly.

Spray {{chicken-wings}} of wings lightly with cooking oil. Preheat the air fryer to 200°C and cook the wings in a single layer for 12 minutes, flip, then cook for 10 more minutes until crisp and golden.

Mix {{gochujang}} of gochujang with {{honey}} of honey, {{soy-sauce-light}} of soy sauce, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, and {{sesame-oil}} of sesame oil. Toss the hot wings in the glaze and return to the air fryer for 2 minutes at 200°C. Scatter with {{sesame-seeds}} of sesame seeds and sliced spring onion before serving.

items.cause: Full 2 tbsp of gochujang in a smaller batch.
items.fix: Gochujang varies in heat level by brand. Start with 1.5 tbsp and taste the sauce before tossing the wings.

items.cause: Final step run longer than 2 minutes.
items.fix: The glaze only needs 2 minutes to set. Longer and the honey chars.

items.symptom: Wings stick to the basket after glazing
items.cause: Glaze drips through the basket mesh.
items.fix: Line the basket with perforated baking paper for the final 2-minute glaze step.

content.text: Korean-style wings have become a fixture on British pub and restaurant menus. Made at home, they cost a fraction of the price and take about half an hour. Good with steamed rice and sliced cucumber.
